# Rules: Documents, spreadsheets, PDF, OCR and media

**Covers:** `documents/`, `excel_worker.py`, `ocr_worker.py`, `media/`, `creative/`, `tools/images.py`, `tools/pixio.py`, `filesearch/`.

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **PDF redaction edits the page; it never regenerates it** (v1.154.0).
  `documents/pdf_redact.py`: pikepdf (MPL-2.0) rewrites the content stream so
  the glyphs are genuinely deleted, pdfplumber supplies word geometry for true
  black boxes, and the written file is RE-READ to prove the values are gone —
  `RedactionUnverified` deletes the output rather than hand back a PDF that
  looks redacted and still carries the SSN. Only then does the old rebuild
  (`write_document` from extracted text) run, and the note says which path
  produced the file. Do not "simplify" this by trusting the transform: matching
  text in content streams is heuristic (values split across operators, odd
  encodings), and the verification is the only thing making it safe. pikepdf is
  a NATIVE wheel and has a `packaging/ironjarvis.spec` entry. Detection also
  runs PER LINE and the address pattern is case-insensitive — both were live
  defects: `\s` separators welded numbers across line breaks (6 of 7 "phone"
  hits on a real return were ownership percentages), and uppercase tax-document
  addresses were never matched at all.

- **A tool that writes a file says WHERE, absolutely** (v1.153.2), and a reply
  that CLAIMS a file is checked against the ledger. Two halves of one live
  report ("it told me it saved the file; the path it gave has no file"):
  (a) `redact_pii`/`write_document`/`convert_document` reported a
  WORKSPACE-RELATIVE path, which is a bare filename whenever the output lands
  in the workspace root — the model relays it and the user looks next to the
  source. They now report the absolute path and carry `abs_path` in `data`.
  (b) `_creation_honesty_note` keys off the USER's phrasing, so "redact this
  K-1" matched nothing and a reply announcing a saved file went unchecked —
  the ledger showed only `redact_scan`, which writes nothing.
  `_claimed_write_note` now judges the reply's own claim against what actually
  ran, in BOTH chat lanes. Note the destinations differ by lane: chat's tool
  workspace is `home/uploads`, an agent session's is its own session dir.

- **Media is QUOTED before it is made, a spend is CARDED, free is free, a
  long render comes home through the daemon** (v1.346.0, the user's
  decisions 2026-10-17: any service — theirs is Pixio — with the door open;
  ask before every spend but a free Maker generation needs no card; notify
  on completion and show the result in the chat; keep the chat UI exactly
  the same). `media/` is the package: `base.py` (Quote {expected_cost,
  currency, free, free_label, provisional, note} + `Quote.words`, JobHandle,
  JobState, `MediaProvider` — every call off the loop and bounded),
  `pixio.py` (free iff `expectedDebit == 0` AND not provisional AND an
  allowance applied / plan-covered; 402/422/429 in plain words carrying
  shortfall/inputHint/Retry-After; Idempotency-Key on start; cheapest model
  by `yourCredits`; models cached 10 min), `openai_images.py` (never free,
  a static list-price table, synchronous b64), `fake.py` (ONLY under
  `IRONJARVIS_MEDIA_FAKE=1`; the integrator's live drive and the tests),
  `registry.py` (`choose` = explicit > `media_provider` setting > the ONLY
  connected > a refusal naming what to connect — TWO connected + "auto"
  REFUSES "pick one", it never guesses; `platform.media`), `pixio_http.py`
  + `deliver.py` (lifted out of tools/pixio.py, which now calls them; CDN
  downloads carry NO headers), `jobs.py` + `models.py` (MediaJobRecord, a
  late model; one tracked task per started job, 2→15 s backoff on an
  injected sleep, `media_job_max_s`; success → deliver → ONE chat line via
  `chat_append` ("Your <kind> is ready." + the image syntax with the
  absolute path in angle brackets, `documents`, `panelKind: media`,
  `mediaJob`) + `media.completed`; failure → the plain-words line +
  `media.failed`; no thread → publish only; boot reconcile re-polls
  queued/running rows by `provider_job_id`, NEVER re-dispatches). Settings
  rows: `media_provider`, `media_ask_when_free`, `media_inline_wait_s`
  (45), `media_job_max_s` (1800), `media_default_models`. THE TOOL
  (`tools/media_tool.generate_media`, ASK tier, IRREVERSIBLE,
  `LOW_TRUST_DENY`, `egress.GENERATES_MEDIA_TOOLS` → a local-only turn
  cards it): `Tool.spend_check(args, ctx) -> SpendCheck {ask, words,
  cost_note} | None` is a NEW generic hook (`spend_checks_for` runs one
  check per call of a round, keyed by the call object): free and not
  `media_ask_when_free` → ask False → the call is GRANTED for this one call
  through `_grant_extra` (the v1.270.1 rule) and the ledger row says
  "free (…)"; paid/unknown → the card with `Quote.words`, `cost_note` on
  the approval frame, in yolo too, past every tab/standing/conversation
  grant, `can_always` False, wider answers read as once; the quote is
  cached 60 s so execute pays no second estimate; execute polls inline up
  to `media_inline_wait_s` else hands the job to MediaJobs with
  `ctx.thread_id` (`ToolContext.thread_id`, set by BOTH chat lanes from
  `body.thread_id` and by the runtime from `options.chat_thread_id`);
  INLINE MEDIA: `media_from_result` + `append_inline_media` put the image
  syntax for every `data.media` path the reply does not already show onto
  the settled reply in BOTH lanes; the runtime's `_pause_needed` consults
  the same hook (the ask carries `cost_note`). `autoselect` ASK-arms it
  from a media-MAKING imperative only ("show me a picture of" / "find an
  image" / "resize the photo" arm nothing). The MOCK adapter calls
  `generate_media` first when it is armed (the live drive + an honest
  first-run demo). DASHBOARD: one `approval-cost` line on ApprovalCard
  (both `useChatStream` reducers whitelist `cost_note`), the bell maps
  `media.completed`/`media.failed` → `/chat?thread=`; the media renders
  through the EXISTING MarkdownMedia path (`/creative/file-by-path`); no
  other UI change. LESSON, third time: the X lane's reviewer died mid-run
  and left a MUTATION APPLIED (`if False:` in `spend_checks_for` — no
  verdict reached any lane; 9 of its own pins red); the integrator caught
  it; the independent re-review (30e2d13f) then found that a round with
  TWO priced generations put up ONE batch card (the v1.247.0 same-
  permission rule) priced for the FIRST call only, and one Allow ran both
  — `tools/base.spend_words_for(checks)` now names each distinct quote
  once ("; "-joined) on the stream frame AND the runtime's merged batch
  pause, lock-step, pinned in both. The POST lane (no cards by design)
  REFUSES a priced verdict ("this lane cannot ask for approval; use the
  chat page") so a raw API caller cannot spend un-carded; a free verdict
  runs. Known: an explicitly armed ask-tier tool is "allow" by overrides
  in the stream lane, so a spend check with NO opinion shows no card —
  `execute` refuses on the same `choose`, so nothing is spent un-carded; a
  batch card still approves N spends with one Allow (honestly priced); a finished job's `cost_note` is the
  charged note, not the quoted words; the agent-runtime ask's cost_note is
  not shown on the polled AgentApprovalRow / mission screen; not proven
  against real Pixio/OpenAI (a real key spends money). Pins: `tests/test_{
  media_providers,media_jobs,generate_media_tool,media_vocab,
  mock_media_call}_v1346.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/media-in-chat-v1346.test.tsx`.
  v1.346.1 (a REAL race behind a "flaky" test): v1.346.0's Tests gate (48-min
  runner) went red on `test_mcp_stdio_transport_v1291`'s kill test — "gave up
  waiting for the wedged grandchild server to die" — and the same test failed
  1 run in 5 locally on unchanged code. `StdioTransport._ensure_started`
  spawned the launcher with a plain `Popen` and assigned the kill-on-close
  Job AFTERWARDS; a grandchild the launcher forked in that window is NOT in
  the Job (assignment never adopts existing children), so
  `TerminateJobObject` killed the launcher and left the real server holding
  the pipe. Now: born with `CREATE_SUSPENDED` → `_win_job_for` → `_resume`
  (the v1.333.0 `core/procs.spawn` shape; a failed resume kills the never-ran
  child and spawns plainly with no Job). Pin:
  `tests/test_mcp_spawn_suspended_v1346.py` (flag + assign-before-resume
  order through spies; the behavioural kill test keeps proving the tree
  dies). Rule: a process you mean to own by Job is CREATED SUSPENDED, never
  adopted after the fact.
  v1.383.1 (test-only, a LEAK the suite made on every run): that pin's spies
  REPLACED the Windows primitives — `_resume` answered True without
  resuming, `_win_job_for` handed back a pretend Job, `_win_terminate_job`
  answered True without ending anything — so its sleeper (really created
  suspended) never ran, `close()` believed the "Job" ended it, and every
  full run left one `python -c "import sys, time; time.sleep(30)"` in the
  Suspended state forever (57 on the user's PC across the main checkout and
  agent worktrees since 2026-10-21). The spies now record and DELEGATE to the
  real functions, and `test_a_closed_server_leaves_no_suspended_or_live_child_
  by_pid` checks every started pid is gone (psutil reads a suspended process
  as `stopped`); four mutations go red (the old spies, a pretend terminate
  alone, a failed resume that no longer kills, `close()` skipping its kill).
  Rule: a spy on a kill, resume or Job primitive RECORDS and calls the real
  one; a fake that answers "done" without doing it leaves a real process
  behind, and a test that starts a real child checks by pid that it is gone.
  v1.347.0 (a USER BUG: "the image was generated, but never appeared back
  in the chat"; it was only in the Creative library). Read off the live
  ledger: a NEW chat's first question goes out BEFORE the page's first save
  names the chat, so `body.thread_id` (→ `ctx.thread_id`) was "" — the job
  finished with `thread_id = ""`, appended nothing, and the bell opened a
  blank `/chat`. FIX: `MediaJobRecord.turn_id` (+ `homed_at`, additive) from
  `ctx.turn_id` (passed only when set — doubles take no kwarg);
  `MediaJobs._home_for` decides the chat AT FINISH (row's thread, else
  `TurnLogs.thread_for(turn)` = live turn or pending `link_later`, else
  `ChatTurnRecord.thread_id`) under `_home_lock`, the SAME lock
  `home_turn(turn, thread)` takes — called by `POST /chat/turns/{id}/thread`
  (answer gains `media_homed`) — so a link either lands first (the finish
  sees it) or after (it delivers the finished, undelivered row itself).
  `home_strays()` runs inside `reconcile_at_boot`: a finished chat job with
  no chat (≤ 14 days, ≤ 50) finds it via `turn_id`, else the ONE linked
  turn record whose `frames_json` holds "(job <id>)" within −2 h/+10 min
  (the v1.346.0 rows; ambiguous = nothing). `chat_append.LINE_KEYS` gained
  `mediaJob` and `_line_key` skips a second line for the same job. The bell
  opens `/creative` for a FINISHED result with no chat. SAME RELEASE, the
  two failed tries before it: Pixio's default model was "cheapest whose
  words say image" — an EDITOR (`image-to-image`, 0 credits) — so
  `media/pixio.model_kind` reads a `<in>-to-<out>` type by its OUTPUT
  (`text-to-audio` is music by id/name words — never "udio", it is inside
  "audio"), `prompt_only(row)` (type `text-to-*`, no editor/reference/lora
  id, every required input in `PROMPT_INPUTS`) filters the default, and
  `MediaProvider.prepare(model, params, kind, has_refs=)` (base: unchanged;
  called in `GenerateMediaTool._resolve` before the quote) prefixes a bare
  id with `pixio/`, refuses unknown / other-kind / needs-more models with up
  to three that work (`_suggest`), and fills a speech model's `text` from
  the prompt; an empty or unreadable catalog checks nothing more. Live
  check (read-only GETs): image → `bria/text-to-image/base`, music →
  `lyria3-clip`; the live DB COPY delivered the user's apple once. Pins:
  `tests/test_media_comes_home_v1347.py` (12 mutations, all red).

- **NO WinRT IN THE DAEMON PROCESS: Windows OCR runs in a killable child**
  (v1.410.2, a USER BUG: "Iron Jarvis isn't responding" after every start).
  `logs/daemon-freeze.txt` (v1.409.1's watcher) showed, in all three frozen
  runs, a pane restore parked in `CreateProcessW` (the Store pwsh) AND the
  OCR self-test (`GET /onboarding` → readiness → doctor `check_local_ocr` →
  `local_ocr.self_test`) parked at its first WinRT object
  (`InMemoryRandomAccessStream()`). A call through the `winrt` bindings HOLDS
  THE GIL while it waits, so a stalled Windows activation stopped every
  thread — loop, `/health`, the freeze watcher's re-arm — and the desktop
  watchdog restarted it into the same freeze. (This is very likely also the
  "cause NOT found" of v1.409.1.) `src/iron_jarvis/ocr_worker.py` is now the
  ONLY module that imports `winrt`; `documents/local_ocr` asks it through
  `_ask_worker` (`core/procs.run`, one JSON request on stdin, killed at
  `deadline * pages + WORKER_START_S`), `languages()`, `recognize_many` (one
  child per document via `local_ocr_many`), `recognize_png`; frozen =
  `ironjarvis.exe ocr-worker` (fast path in `packaging/ironjarvis_entry.py`,
  identical to the hidden CLI subcommand), source = `python -m
  iron_jarvis.ocr_worker`. A self-test whose worker did not answer says "Windows
  OCR did not answer" and is NOT cached. Chat asks `available()` through
  `asyncio.to_thread`. RULE: any native binding that can block inside
  Windows (WinRT, COM activation) runs in a child process, never in the
  daemon — a GIL-holding wait cannot be bounded from inside the process.
  Pins: `tests/test_ocr_isolation_v14102.py` (a worker that holds ITS OWN GIL
  forever: this process's heartbeat keeps ticking; a fresh daemon process has
  never loaded `winrt` after a real self-test); `test_local_ocr_scans` seams
  moved to `local_ocr_many` / `_ask_worker` / `_worker_argv`. SAME RELEASE:
  `background-layer-v1410` no longer spies on the frame's `contentWindow`
  (CI's jsdom replaced the window after the spy went on; v1.410.0 and
  v1.410.1 published nothing because of it) — it reads the layer's own
  `data-running` / `data-motion` and pins `backgroundMessages` as a function.

- **Spreadsheets are WORKED OUT by Iron Jarvis, checked against Excel
  itself; results are kept IN the file; every stated figure has a
  calculator** (v1.465.0; the owner: "expertly handle excel spread sheets …
  full formulas, placement of data, overall spreadsheet context, mathematical
  accuracy, formatting and purpose").
  - **The engine (`documents/excel_formula.py`, rebuilt, same public API:
    `FormulaError`, `Grid`, `evaluate_formula`).**
    - The parser builds THUNKS, so `IF`/`IFERROR`/`IFNA`/`AND`/`OR`/
      `ISERROR`/`ISNA` (`_LAZY`) work out only what they take.
    - `Grid.get` answers the saved value, else COMPUTES the cell's formula
      (memo, `_stack` circle check → "circular reference at X", `_MAX_DEPTH`,
      a per-formula read budget `_reads` the caller resets). `Grid.saved` is
      the value Excel saved and nothing else: `excel_formula_check` compares
      against THAT, never against the engine's own answer.
    - `SUPPORTED` (80 functions). Defined names, whole columns (`A:A`,
      bounded by the sheet's rows), sheet names matched without case.
      `ExcelError(code)` is an Excel error VALUE a formula produced.
    - `Grid(None)` is the calculator's grid (`variables`, no cells).
  - **THE GROUND TRUTH IS EXCEL.** `tests/fixtures/excel_truth_v1465/`
    holds `cov.xlsx` (every function), `books.xlsx` (a small business
    workbook with six planted mistakes) and `excel_truth.json`: what the
    real Excel on the owner's PC answered for all 318 formula cells (hidden,
    read-only, through COM). `tests/test_excel_engine_v1465.py` replays it;
    a pin fails when a `SUPPORTED` function is not in it. The first run
    found three faults, each now a rule:
    - Excel keeps 15 significant digits: `excel_round` rounds
      `f"{v:.15g}"` half AWAY from zero (750*7.25% → 54.38, never
      Python's 54.37), and `_rank` compares numbers at 15 digits
      (`0.1+0.2=0.3` is TRUE).
    - A leading minus binds tighter than `^` and `^` is left to right
      (`=-2^2` is 4, `=2^3^2` is 64): `_multiplicative` → `_power` →
      `_unary` → `_percent`.
    - A newer function written plainly opens in Excel as `#NAME?`.
      `for_file()` adds the file's prefix (`_PREFIXED`: `_xlfn.` /
      `_xlfn._xlws.`), never inside quotes; `for_reading()` removes it.
      EVERY place that writes a formula calls `for_file`: `excel_edit`,
      `writers._xlsx_fill` and the plain-rows branch, `excel_apply_spec`. A
      NEW function added to `SUPPORTED` that Excel 2007 lacks needs a
      `_PREFIXED` row and a fixture row answered by Excel.
  - **Results kept in the file (`documents/excel_recalc.py`).**
    `compute_missing(path, sheets)` works out every formula cell with no
    saved result (bounded: `MAX_FILE_BYTES`, `MAX_FORMULAS`, `DEADLINE_S`;
    `Recalc.values` shows a date cell as an ISO date; `failed` names each
    cell and why; never raises). `has_formulas(path)` scans the sheets' XML
    for a formula tag FIRST (a 100,000-row sheet of plain numbers cost a 16 s
    load after every write to learn there was nothing to do; 0.08 s now), and
    `too_large` refuses a whole load past `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (12 MB) or
    `MAX_CELLS` (400,000; `cell_estimate` = the larger of the sheets' stated
    size and their XML bytes / 40, because a workbook written as a stream
    states no size). A new whole-workbook load (`Grid(path)`) goes behind
    both. `store_results(path)` then writes each
    result into the sheet XML beside its `<f>` (regex over what the library
    writes; `t="str"` / `t="b"`), into a copy named
    `.recalc-<pid>-<name>` (the library opens a file by its extension),
    reads the copy back (`_stored_reads_back`) and only then `os.replace`s.
    It touches ONLY a workbook whose `xl/workbook.xml` says
    `fullCalcOnLoad="1"` (what openpyxl writes), so Excel recalculates
    everything on open and a stored number can never mask Excel's own.
    Called after `excel_edit`, `write_document` (.xlsx,
    `writers._xlsx_store_results`) and `excel_apply_spec`. An error result
    is never stored.
  - **Tools (`documents/excel_tools.py`).**
    - `excel_edit` returns `results [{sheet, cell, formula, value|error}]`
      and one output line per formula it wrote; takes formatting keys
      (`_FORMAT_KEYS`: number_format, bold, italic, fill, font_color, align,
      wrap; a formatting-only edit may name a range and writes NO value).
    - `write_document` of an .xlsx appends `excel_map.written_summary`
      (formula count, ≤ 8 totals with values, ≤ 6 WORTH A LOOK lines;
      `data["workbook"]`): the model's own workbook is reviewed in the answer
      to the write. A workbook with no formula adds nothing.
    - `Grid._peek` reads a cell without creating it (asking openpyxl for a
      missing cell makes one and grows `max_row`).
    - `excel_read` (values) and `excel_query` (`_load_table_computed`) fill
      unsaved formulas through `fill_rows`; `worked_out` /
      `FORMULAS_WORKED_OUT_NOTE` say so; `FORMULAS_LEFT_OUT_NOTE` is only
      for cells the engine could not work out.
    - `excel_query`: groups ranked by ABSOLUTE size, the cut said with its
      sum, "Total of all N group(s)", `groups_total`, limit ≤ 200; dates
      compared as dates (`_as_date`); `_fmt_num` never rounds a difference
      away.
    - `excel_profile` returns `documents/excel_map.workbook_map` (header
      row, column kinds and formats, `formula_pattern` groups, totals with
      values, `uses_sheets`, names, hidden sheets, `looks_like` from the
      sheet's own words, and `checks`: typed number in a formula column,
      pattern break, SUM stopping short, typed total ≠ the block above,
      numbers stored as text, formulas that come to an error). The first
      line per sheet is the old headline. A map that raises falls back to
      the quick profile (`data.quick`).
  - **`calculate` (`documents/calculate_tool.py`):** allow tier, READONLY,
    no file. Expressions in order (≤ 40); a one-word label becomes a NAME
    for later ones (never a cell-like label). On every built-in agent's
    roster (`agents/types.py`). In chat it is armed in its OWN place,
    outside the six-tool cap, in `chat_turn._resolve_armed_tools` beside the
    settings tools, when `autoselect.wants_calculator(text, picked)` says so
    (arithmetic asked outright, or a document tool picked AND a money word).
    Past the six-tool cap, but NEVER past a weak model's own tool budget:
    when the envelope narrowed `_ceiling` it takes a place only if one is
    free (`test_chat_envelope_v1202` went red on GitHub when it did not).
    `session_result` gained `ended_on_failed_change`, so the two recorded
    receipt fixtures were regenerated (`IJ_REGEN_RECEIPT_SEAMS=1`,
    `IJ_REGEN_RUN_WHERE_DISPATCHED=1`): a NEW key on `session_result` always
    means regenerating both.
    It is NOT in `AUTO_SAFE_TOOLS` and no rule scores it:
    `select_auto_tools` is byte-identical (eight pins of its exact output
    went red when the calculator was first added inside it).
  - **Also in this release.** `writers.UNWRITABLE_FORMATS` (.xls, .doc,
    .rtf, …) are refused with nothing written. Rows written to a PDF are a
    table (`_table_rows`), a tab is four spaces, and `_undrawable` replaces
    a character the font lacks with "?" and warns. A coding helper
    (`HELPER_ORIGIN`) is `completed_with_failures` only when
    `session_result["ended_on_failed_change"]` (its LAST non-read-only call
    failed; `Orchestrator._settle_finished_run`); replayed read-only on the
    owner's ledger: 53 labelled, 5 kept. Every other origin keeps the old
    rule. `core/model_cwd.remap(raw, workspace)`: an absolute path inside
    claude-cli's scratch cwd (`<temp>/ironjarvis-claude-cwd*`, which the CLI
    tells its model is the working directory) is read as the same relative
    path in the workspace, in `tools/base.safe_path` and the three
    `_resolve_read_path`s (documents, excel, images); pure text, a path
    with `..` is left alone.
  - **LIVE-PROVEN** (scratch daemon on 8797, real claude-cli Haiku, judged by
    the files): a client memo with 12 of 12 money figures right (3 were wrong
    on v1.464.0); a review that found all six planted mistakes with the right
    cells once `excel_profile` was armed (without it, one wrong cell); a
    model-built workbook whose 39 stored results all equalled real Excel's.
  - **Pins:** `tests/test_excel_engine_v1465.py`,
    `tests/test_excel_tools_v1465.py`, `tests/test_office_fixes_v1465.py`;
    moved on purpose: `test_excel_formula_skills` (VLOOKUP and whole columns
    work now), `test_office_edge_cases_v1464` (the total is the true 42; an
    edit keeps results in the file), both tool-word fixtures.
  - **To refresh the Excel fixture** (needs Excel): build the workbooks,
    run a PowerShell COM script that opens each read-only in its own hidden
    Excel, `CalculateFull()`, and dumps every formula cell's `Value2` to
    JSON; close only the Excel it started.
  - **OPEN:** array formulas, INDIRECT, OFFSET and links to other
    workbooks are named and left for Excel; `TEXT` knows a few formats;
    `convert_document` xlsx → csv still blanks unsaved formulas; an agent
    run's own arithmetic depends on the model calling `calculate`.

- **Live Excel: the workbook OPEN in Excel is reached through ONE short-lived
  child; a change is all-or-nothing, listed, undoable, and never saved**
  (v1.466.0; the owner: "edit a live excel file with parity to the claude excel
  extension"; measured on Excel 16.0 build 20527 with a hidden Excel the tests
  start themselves).
  - **The child (`src/iron_jarvis/excel_worker.py`).** The ONLY module that
    imports `pythoncom` / `win32com` (pinned). A COM call into Excel can wait
    forever (a dialog box, a cell being typed in), so the v1.410.2 rule holds:
    `documents/excel_live._ask_worker` starts `ironjarvis.exe excel-worker`
    (fast path in `packaging/ironjarvis_entry.py`; hidden CLI subcommand;
    source: `python -m iron_jarvis.excel_worker`) through `core/procs.run`,
    one JSON request on stdin, one JSON answer, killed at its deadline.
    pywin32 is a declared win32 dependency and a `hiddenimports` block in the
    spec. It NEVER starts Excel (it attaches through the running object table:
    `_apps()`, front-most first), never opens, saves or closes a workbook,
    and touches only `DisplayAlerts`, in a `finally`, for a sheet delete.
  - **Requests:** `look` (open workbooks, sheets, selection, a range's values
    and formulas), `snapshot` (`SaveCopyAs` into a folder, named after the
    workbook; the workbook's Saved flag and path are untouched, measured),
    `plan` (checks every step, counts what it would overwrite, changes
    nothing), `apply`, `restore`, `goto`. Excel's error values arrive as
    negative integers (`ERROR_NAMES`); numbers as floats; dates through
    `.Value` as datetimes.
  - **`apply` is ALL OR NOTHING.** Every step is checked first (`planning`);
    then each step writes what it is about to replace to the undo file
    (`<home>/excel-live/undo/<change id>.jsonl`) BEFORE it runs and its
    after-state after; a step that fails makes `_restore_file(forgiving=True)`
    put the earlier ones back. A step written down and then refused by Excel
    has no `after` row and is NOT "could not be put back" (a refused delete
    read as half-done until the real-Excel test caught it). A child stopped
    at its deadline is rolled back by the tool with a forgiving `restore`.
  - **A step must say its sheet** (`Cx.sheet`): on the step, as
    `Sheet!A1:D9` (`split_sheet`), or one `sheet` for the whole call. In the
    first live trial a model that had just read Sales sorted the ACTIVE sheet.
    A step may use a sheet an earlier step of the same call makes
    (`_Deferred`, `Cx.pending`).
  - **Undo** (`UNDO_KIND` "excel_live_restore"): `capture_undo` mints the
    change id and the undo file's path (the pdf_tools `id(args)` hand-off);
    `routes/undo.perform_undo` has its own branch (no tool permission asked,
    like `record_restore`); `GET /config/changes/{id}` lists the kind; the
    chat's change card is the existing one (`chat_turn.config_cards_from_result`
    reads `data["excel_change"]`). `restore` puts a cell back only while it
    still holds what the change left (`after`), names what it left alone, and
    reverses structure by exact inverses (inserted lines only while empty; a
    colour rule by count; a chart, table or pivot by name). Deleting rows,
    columns or a sheet has NO inverse: a copy of the workbook is saved to
    `excel-live/copies/` first and the tool's output says in capitals that it
    cannot be undone (a model repeated "you can undo this" after a delete).
  - **Cards.** `excel_live_look` allow (READONLY, untrusted content);
    `excel_live_edit` ask (reversible, untrusted: its answer quotes cells).
    `spend_check` asks the child for the plan (cached 20 s, so card + change
    are one `plan` and one `apply`): a destructive step is once-only in every
    posture; more than `OVERWRITE_CARD_CELLS` (10) data cells replaced, or any
    formula replaced by a plain value, cards past a chat's grant
    (`dont_ask_skips`); anything else follows the ordinary ask tier.
  - **Arming.** `autoselect.wants_live_excel(text, excel_open, has_files)`:
    the open workbook said outright, or spreadsheet talk while
    `excel_live.excel_seen()` (a remembered process check, refreshed in the
    background, never waits) and no file attached or named. `K1`, `W2`, `Q3`
    are not cell references; only `cell B4` or a range with a colon counts.
    `_resolve_armed_tools` arms the look in its own place under the ceiling
    (both lanes); the STREAM lane alone ask-arms the edit. Neither is on a
    roster (`_OFF_ROSTER_BY_DESIGN`).
  - **Honesty.** A refusal that left the workbook untouched starts
    `UNCHANGED_LEAD` ("NOTHING WAS CHANGED in the workbook."); both lanes
    append `excel_live.unchanged_note(turn_id, tools_used)` when a turn tried
    a change and none landed (decided from what ran, never from the reply);
    `excel_live_edit` is in `_CHANGES_A_FILE_UNNAMED`.
  - **File tools read the open workbook** through `path: "live:<name>"`
    (`excel_tools._read_target` → `excel_live.live_path`: a copy under
    `excel-live/snap/<id>/<Workbook name>`, swept after ten minutes). The
    source's folder is checked against the folders Jarvis may read.
  - **REVIEW (v1.466.0, an independent reviewer; 30+ defects, each pinned
    in the real-Excel file or the stand-in file; 81 mutations, 73 red, 5 more
    pinned after, 3 equivalent).** What the code now guarantees:
    - **Undo puts back exactly what was there.** Values are written back as
      what they WERE (text "00123" stays text, "1/2" is not a date; formats
      and a date string's format restored; spilled formulas and `=UNIQUE()`
      come back as written, never `=@...`; a range of several colours keeps
      each cell's colour; a format the user changed afterwards is left).
    - **Undo never hits another target.** A step's undo record is by the
      cells as they are AFTER later steps of the same call moved them (set
      B6 then delete row 2); with the original workbook closed, Undo by name
      refuses a same-named workbook from another folder (`_find_book(...,
      exact=True)`; never falls back from an unsaved Book1 to a saved one).
    - **Rows hidden by a filter** (`FILTER_WORDS`, code `filtered`): a block
      write, clear, sort or Undo across filter-hidden rows is REFUSED (Excel
      skips hidden rows, so values land on the wrong rows). `clear_filter`
      earlier in the same call lifts it (`Cx.unfiltered`).
    - **A sort takes the whole table:** sorting part of a table's columns is
      refused (`partial_sort`) unless the step says `"alone": true`. Undo of
      a sort restores rows, fills and notes (found by halving, not cell by
      cell); NOT validation rules, hyperlinks or row heights. Undo of
      `filter` removes it and does not restore earlier criteria.
    - **"Nothing was changed" is true:** a refused pivot no longer clears
      the user's own pivot table; a refused `add_sheet` leaves no stray
      sheet; a step refused on a protected sheet is not "half done".
    - **A deletion is carded by its STEPS** (`is_destructive(args["ops"])`),
      whatever Excel answered to the plan (busy, or a workbook Jarvis may not
      read), and a rename followed by a deletion on the new name is seen.
      `SpendCheck.irreversible` (tools/base.py, read by routes/chat.py and
      agents/runtime.py) keeps "You can undo this" off such a card.
    - **The change lands in the workbook the card named**
      (`ExcelLiveEditTool._targets`: the plan's path is kept per call).
    - **A workbook in a folder Jarvis may not read** is named and nothing
      else (`hide_unreadable`: no sheets, tables or selection; a refused plan
      quotes none of its headings; `look range=selection` for a workbook not
      in front no longer returns another workbook's cells). `_read_refusal`
      fails closed. OneDrive / SharePoint (https) paths are not judged.
    - **A formula that makes Excel reach outside** is refused
      (`excel_worker.reaches_out`: WEBSERVICE, RTD, IMAGE, CALL, REGISTER.ID,
      SQL.REQUEST, a DDE link, a web address or network share outside
      quotes; linear). v1.469.0 applies the same rule to saved files.
    - **Arming** (`wants_live_excel`): "cell phone", "current range", "excel
      at", an IRS worksheet and "make me a spreadsheet" arm nothing; "this
      formula", "#REF!", "column C" do.
    - AutoSave: the answer says Excel saves by itself within seconds (it had
      said "has already saved").
  - **Kept data.** `<home>/excel-live/` (undo 30 days, copies 14 days, snap
    10 minutes; `sweep`, which runs only on the next live call, so a copy can outlast its age until then) is left out of backups. It holds client data.
  - **Tests.** `tests/test_excel_live_v1466.py` (no Excel: the child is a
    stand-in); `tests/test_excel_live_real_v1466.py` (the REAL Excel, only
    with `IJ_LIVE_EXCEL=1`: run it on this PC after any change to the child).
    conftest sets `IRONJARVIS_EXCEL_LIVE=off` and `IRONJARVIS_EXCEL_SEEN=0`:
    no test may look into the developer's own Excel.
  - **RELEASE CHECK:** `"<install>\resources\daemon\ironjarvis.exe"
    excel-worker` fed `{"op": "look"}` on stdin must answer one JSON line
    with `"ok": true`.
  - **OPEN:** Excel's own Ctrl+Z after a change was not measured (assumed
    cleared, and said so); typing-in-a-cell and Protected View refusals are
    written from Excel's documented error codes, not driven; no panel inside
    Excel; agents and the POST lane cannot change a workbook.

- **Matching two lists of transactions in whole cents; Excel's own features
  in a SAVED workbook; what only Excel can do safely is refused** (v1.469.0;
  step 5 of the live-Excel plan).
  - **`documents/excel_reconcile.py`, tool `excel_reconcile`** (allow tier;
    REVERSIBLE only because `save_as` writes a NEW .xlsx in the workspace,
    undo kind `file_delete`, an existing file refused; untrusted content; on
    the rosters beside `excel_trace`). Each side is `{path (a file or
    live:<name>), sheet?, amount | money_in + money_out, date?, ref?,
    description?, header_row?, flip?}` read through `_load_table_computed`
    (unsaved formulas worked out; `MAX_ROWS` 50,000, said when cut).
    `to_cents` rounds the way Excel shows a number (15 significant digits,
    half away from zero) and reads "1,234.50", "(45.00)", "$12", "15.00-".
    PASSES, each row matched at most once: amount + reference (`norm_ref`:
    no case, punctuation or leading zeros), amount + dates within
    `date_window_days` (default 5; inside one amount both lists are walked in
    date order, `_walk`, which finds the MOST pairs: pinned against a
    brute-force answer), amount alone only when a list has no date column,
    then `tolerance`. NEVER matched, only listed: the same amount outside the
    window (`near`), one row equal to several unmatched rows of one day on
    the other side (`groups`). `opposite_signs` is noticed, never applied.
  - **THE PROOF IS AN INVARIANT:** `totals()` gives `difference` (total A −
    total B) and `explained` (only-in-A − only-in-B + differences inside
    tolerance pairs); they are equal for any lists (300 random cases pinned,
    with "no row lost, invented or matched twice"). The answer prints "It
    ties" from that comparison, never from a claim.
  - **`documents/excel_features.py`** (`excel_edit` `features`): steps with
    the LIVE tool's names and fields (pinned against `excel_live._EDIT_HELP`):
    `FEATURE_OPS` conditional_format, validation, freeze, column_width,
    autofit (by text length; a saved file has no Excel to measure fonts, and
    the answer says so), name, table, note, print_setup. `NEEDS_EXCEL`
    (insert/delete rows and columns, sort, filter, rename_sheet, delete_sheet,
    pivot, chart, refresh) is refused by `check_features` BEFORE the workbook
    is opened: openpyxl adjusts no references, so those would leave formulas
    pointing at the wrong cells. A step that fails raises `FeatureRefused`
    before `wb.save`, so the file is byte-identical (pinned by hash) and the
    answer ends "Nothing was changed."; only `FeatureRefused` gets those
    words, every other error keeps `_open_error`. A step never guesses its
    sheet (the call's `sheet`, `Sheet!A1`, or a one-sheet workbook). Formula
    results are stored again after the save (`store_results`).
  - **Checked in the real Excel**
    (`tests/test_excel_features_real_v1469.py`, `IJ_LIVE_EXCEL=1`): the saved

    rule is read through `DisplayFormat` cell by cell, the dropdowns through

  - **A formula that would reach OUTSIDE the workbook is never written to

    through (`excel_edit` formulas AND text values starting with "=",

    it raises `OutsideFormula` and nothing is saved. A new place that writes

  - **The edit tool is OFFERED for these steps.**
    `autoselect.wants_excel_features(text, picked)` arms `excel_edit` (in

  - **LIVE-PROVEN** (scratch daemon on 8797, Excel helper off, real

  - **Arming:** `autoselect.wants_excel_reconcile(text, picked)` only beside

  - **Skills:** the starter `bank-reconciliation-review` and
    `variance-analysis` name the new tools (still five skills per bundle,

  - **Pins:** `tests/test_excel_reconcile_v1469.py`,
    `tests/test_excel_features_v1469.py`,
    `tests/test_excel_features_real_v1469.py`.
  - **REVIEW (v1.467.0 to v1.469.0, an independent reviewer; 8 commits, each
    defect red first, the Excel cases compared with its own hidden Excel).**
    - **Matching:** `to_cents` reads a comma only as a thousands comma (a
      decimal comma is NOT read and the row is named); "$ (12.00)" and
      "- 12.00" are read; out of range never raises. A reference seen more
      than once on a side pairs only inside the date window, in date order.
      The tolerance never pairs opposite signs. `read_side` says: unreadable
      amounts, rows with no date, a last row equal to the sum above it
      (`last_row` leaves it out), a money-out column written in negatives.
      `write_result` forces every cell to text and cleans sheet titles.
      `excel_reconcile` is in `_FILE_CHANGING_TOOLS`, `STRICT_ASK_TOOLS` and
      `_RESULT_FILE_TOOLS` (its saved file is a document of the turn; no
      false "nothing was written" note).
    - **Outside formulas:** `reaches_out` takes off `_xlfn.` first and reads
      a single-quoted sheet name as one piece; `write_document` plain text
      for an .xlsx goes through `for_file`.
    - **Tracing:** `_typed` reads a what-if value as a typed cell would hold
      it (date, percent, exponent, TRUE/FALSE; a formula refused). Goal seek
      closes a side it cannot work out and searches the other, under
      `DEADLINE_S`. Following cells uses `_CellIndex` and one deadline
      (57,000 formulas: 115 s to 2.7 s); when it cannot follow to the end it
      says "name the cells to watch". `how` reads the first 2,000 cells of a
      range. `Grid.max_row`/`max_col` reach cells a what-if set below the
      data (whole-column formulas). ARRAY FORMULAS: `Grid.array_formula`,
      `array_filled`, `array_stale`; a cell resting on an array formula the
      change reaches gets a problem line and NO figure (INDIRECT, OFFSET or a
      table column counts as reached); goal seek refuses in words. With no
      what-if in place the engine reads exactly as before (pinned).
    - **Features:** refused before the save, because Excel would not open the
      file: a name equal to a table's, a name or table called c, R, RC, R1C1,
      a table whose heading holds a formula or that lies over the sheet's
      filter or merged cells; a name differing only by case replaces the old
      one. `_autofit_cells` walks only cells that exist. Any other error in a

    - **Dashboard:** `excelUseChosen()`; the stored key is "1", "0" or

  - **v1.469.1 (the owner's decision 2026-11-10: "Yes, restrict it"): a
    link to ANOTHER WORKBOOK is written only when Jarvis may read that
    workbook.** Linking workbooks is everyday accounting, so a link is
    still an ordinary formula and `reaches_out` says nothing about it
    (the first reviewer's pin in `test_excel_live_v1466` stands). The
    folder question is asked separately:
    - `excel_worker.workbook_links(text)` only READS the links (pure,
      linear, `MAX_LINKS` 50): `{dir, file, index}` for
      `'C:\dir\[b.xlsx]S'!A1`, `[b.xlsx]S!A1`, `'C:\dir\b.xlsx'!Name`,
      `'b.xlsx'!Name` and a saved file's own `[1]S!A1` (`index`). Text in
      double quotes, a table column (`Table1[Amount]`) and a 3-D range
      (`'Jan:Dec'!A1`) are not links.
    - `excel_formula.link_reason(formula, open_books=None)` judges them
      (BLOCKING when a link names a folder; never raises; a check that
      fails is a refusal): a full folder through `fs_policy.fs_read_ok`
      (the folder limits AND the protected folders); `//host` refused by
      its text before anything is looked up (`LINK_NETWORK`); a relative
      folder or `[n]` refused only while `fs_policy.read_limits_set()`
      (`LINK_UNCHECKED`); a file name alone judged by where that workbook
      is open from when `open_books` ({lower-cased name: path}) knows it,
      else ordinary (a workbook beside the saved file).
    - `for_file` raises `OutsideFormula` on it, so every formula written
      to a saved file is covered (edits, features, `write_document`,
      `excel_apply_spec`).
    - `excel_live.link_refusal(ops)` runs in `ExcelLiveEditTool.execute`
      after the plan and BEFORE the apply (the child has no config, so the
      rule lives in the daemon): `formula_entries(ops)` reads every step
      entry Excel could take as a formula (a field outside `_TEXT_FIELDS`
      gets its "="; `MAX_STEP_ENTRIES` 5,000); steps with no link ask
      Excel nothing more; a link by name costs ONE plain `look` (names and
      places, no range); Excel silent under a limit is a refusal.
    - INDIRECT builds its reference from TEXT (measured in the real Excel:
      `=INDIRECT("[Jones.xlsx]Summary!B4")` and `=INDIRECT(E1)` both show an
      open workbook's figure), so no reader of links can see where it
      points. `excel_live.uses_indirect(entry)`: while
      `read_limits_set()`, a step that calls INDIRECT costs one `look` and
      is refused when ANY workbook is open in Excel from a place
      `_read_refusal` refuses ("INDIRECT could read Jones.xlsx, open in
      Excel from a folder Jarvis may not read"); Excel silent = refused.
      With no limit set INDIRECT asks Excel nothing. Also measured: a link
      with an allowed path whose file NAME matches a workbook open from
      elsewhere does NOT bind to that workbook (Excel shows #REF!), so the
      path check is enough for a link that names its folder.
    - With no folder limit set and no protected folder named, behaviour is
      exactly as before (pinned).
    - Pins: `tests/test_excel_workbook_links_v14691.py` (28 mutations, 27
      red; the survivor is a second cap), and against the real Excel
      `tests/test_excel_workbook_links_real_v14691.py` (`IJ_LIVE_EXCEL=1`;
      three workbooks open in the test's own hidden Excel).
    - OPEN: under a limit a saved file's own `[1]` link is refused even
      when the workbook it points at is readable (its target is not
      looked up); a link by name in a SAVED file is not judged (Excel
      binds it to a workbook beside the file, or to an open workbook of
      that name); a junction inside a readable folder is followed, as for
      every file tool; INDIRECT in a SAVED file is not judged (it reaches
      only a workbook the user has open when they open the file); text
      written into a cell that an INDIRECT ALREADY in the workbook reads is
      not judged (a workbook's own formulas are the user's).
  - **OPEN:** European number formats are left out and said, not read.

    never `console.warn` (pinned), and `openPopout` must keep its exact
    `savePopoutBounds(userDataDir, route, …)` line (pinned).
  - **NOT BUILT, the owner's call: a task pane inside Excel.** Office loads
    an add-in only from an HTTPS address whose certificate Windows trusts;
    for a localhost app that means installing a root certificate and
    registering the add-in with Office (a trusted catalog or a registry
    key): security settings Iron Jarvis does not change by itself.
  - **Pins:** `tests/test_excel_beside_v1468.py`,
    `dashboard/__tests__/excel-now-{strip,page}-v1468.test.tsx`, the
    names-only case in `tests/test_excel_trace_real_v1467.py` (10 mutations,
    all red).
  - **OPEN:** the beside window was not driven in the packaged desktop app
    (its placement rule and IPC are pinned under node and by source); its
    first place is remembered, so a later press from another screen opens
    where it was left; the selection sent with a message is the one at the
    last read (the block tells the model to read it again); Chat › Code and
    the Build pane chat have no Excel line.

- **How a number is built, what-if, goal seek, and a cell the user can jump
  to** (v1.467.0; step 3 of the live-Excel plan).
  - **`documents/excel_trace.py`, tool `excel_trace`** (allow, READONLY,
    untrusted content, on every built-in roster): modes `how` (precedents down
    to typed-in inputs, `MAX_DEPTH` 6, `MAX_NODES` 120, a range shows its
    first `MAX_RANGE_SHOWN` 4 cells), `affects` (dependents), `what_if`
    (`set` {cell: value}, `watch` cells; with no watch, the END results the
    changed cells lead to, at most `MAX_DEFAULT_WATCH` 12), `goal_seek`
    (bracket outward, then bisection; `exact` False + a "NOT EXACT" line when
    a rounded figure makes the target move in steps). `path` may be
    `live:<name>` (the open workbook, through `excel_tools._read_target`).
  - **The engine (`documents/excel_formula.Grid`)** gained `overrides`
    ({(sheet lower-cased, col, row): value}), `fresh` (work every formula out
    even when Excel saved a result: a saved result does not know about an
    override), `canon()` and `reset()`. Both off = `get` exactly as before.
    A what-if ALWAYS first works the baseline out with `fresh` and compares it
    with what Excel saved; a cell where the two differ, or that cannot be
    worked out, gets a `problem` and NO figure.
  - **Checked against Excel:** `tests/test_excel_trace_real_v1467.py`
    (`IJ_LIVE_EXCEL=1`; its own hidden Excel) sets the what-if values in the
    real Excel and compares every watched cell to 1e-9, compares goal seek
    with Excel's own `GoalSeek`, and drives the jump. A formula that names a
    sheet which does not exist yet is saved by Excel as a link to ANOTHER
    workbook (`[1]Costs!C2`): build sheets before the formulas that read them.
  - **Arming** (`tools/autoselect`): `wants_excel_trace(text, picked)` only
    beside a spreadsheet tool the turn already has (`_TRACE_CARRIERS`), and
    `live_excel_companions(text)` (trace, `excel_query`) ride with
    `excel_live_look`; each only while the ceiling has room
    (`chat_turn._resolve_armed_tools`).
  - **Jump to the cell.** A reply names a cell as a markdown link whose
    address is only a fragment, `#excel/<workbook>/<sheet>/<cell>`
    (`excel_live.cell_link` / `link_hint`, appended to a live look's, a live
    edit's and a live trace's answer; `CELL_LINK_PREFIX` and `CELL_RX` are
    twinned in `dashboard/lib/excelCellLink.ts`, pinned equal). The ONE
    markdown renderer draws it as `components/ExcelCellLink.tsx`, a button
    that posts `POST /excel/live/goto {workbook, sheet, cell}`
    (`routes/documents.py`; `excel_live.clean_cell_target` refuses anything
    that is not a workbook name, a sheet name and a cell before the child is
    asked; 409 with the child's own words). The child's `goto` selects the
    range and brings Excel forward; it refuses a hidden sheet, never opens a
    file, and leaves the workbook's Saved flag alone (measured).
    `excel_live_look` takes `show: true` for "take me there".
  - **Pins:** `tests/test_excel_trace_v1467.py`,
    `tests/test_excel_trace_real_v1467.py`,
    `dashboard/__tests__/excel-cell-link-v1467.test.tsx`.
  - **OPEN:** a what-if is Jarvis's engine, so a cell that uses a function
    outside `SUPPORTED` gets no figure; data tables and scenarios are not
    read; a model must write the link (a raw space in a name breaks it, so the
    hint says %20); a closed file has no jump.

- `documents/` — `pdf_classify.py` is the per-PAGE scan router (v1.176.0,
  wraps the MIT `pdf-inspector` Rust extension). It answers "which pages of
  this PDF are scans", which `looks_scanned_pdf` structurally cannot: that
  asks ONE question of the whole file, so a native-text return with a scanned
  K-1 stapled in at page 12 reads as fully readable and the scan is silently
  invisible. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT and must survive any edit:
  `needs_ocr` ORs the classifier with the old heuristic and never ANDs, an
  empty plan falls back to harvesting rather than to harvesting nothing, and
  every entry point returns `None` (never raises) so an absent or broken
  extension degrades to exactly the v1.174.0 behaviour. A classifier may make
  the app read MORE of a client's document, never less. It is a NATIVE wheel:
  `packaging/ironjarvis.spec` entry + a RECOMMENDED `doctor` check, because a
  packaged build that dropped it would degrade silently forever (the pikepdf
  lesson). Cache version bumped to 2 — v1 records covered the first N pages
  and serving one for a mixed file would freeze that blindness in permanently.
  Also: readers (extract_text: pdf/docx/xlsx/pptx/csv/text/images),
  writers (markdown-AWARE rich creation: headings/lists/tables/code become
  real structure in docx/pdf/pptx/html; xlsx multi-sheet dict + formulas),
  markdown.py (the shared block parser), tools (read/write/extract_pdf/
  convert_document). `tools/images.py` — view_image (vision via the router),
  image_convert/resize/info (Pillow). `tools/pixio.py` — generative media.

- **PDF redaction reads and clears FORM FIELDS too, and proves it over every string in the file** (v1.499.3 review). A filled field's value (`/V`), its drawn appearance (`/AP`), note text and XFA data are scanned; a found value is masked in the field and its appearance dropped; the check after writing reads page text plus fields, appearances, notes and metadata, and never says "verified gone" over a value it did not read (a filled SSN survived before). Nothing found = a byte-for-byte copy, said so. PDF passwords are blanked by `redact_args` before the ledger; CRLF text is written once (no doubled carriage returns) and delimited text becomes columns; a `.doc` converts in a temp folder removed after reading (no client copy left in %TEMP%); uploads never overwrite one another; "Save a copy" refuses a name that leaves the folder. Pins: `tests/test_review_fixes_documents_v1499_3.py`.

- **A figure's link comes only from Iron Jarvis's own record of the read: a reader returns a `source_map`, the registry turns it into marks after the call's ledger row, and both chat lanes link the model's own words, never its notes** (v1.549.0, idea 30-a). `documents/sources.py` (the rule, `link_reply`, `SourceTurn`), `documents/source_store.py` (`sourcemark`, a late model; swept with its chat by `routes/chat.delete_thread` unless `kept`; a new chat's first turn is homed by `POST /chat/turns/{id}/thread` and `link_live_turn`, and a link that lands BEFORE the turn's `SourceTurn` is made waits for it (`sources._WAITING`, at most 200; the page saves a new chat before it sends, so this is the common order); rows with no chat go after 2 days, on the next write), `documents/page_image.py` (pypdfium2 under one lock, pdfplumber word boxes; a line it cannot find is printed ABOVE the page, never boxed by guess). `core/numbers.py` is the one number reader (recaps use it): a figure under 100 or a bare year counts only with a currency sign, a percent sign or decimals; a number glued to letters or joined to digits by `-`, `/`, `:` is not a figure. Readers: `read_document` / `extract_pdf` (`extract_text(layout=)` gives page, paragraph and row offsets; the TEXT the model gets is byte-identical, and marks never change what is read), `excel_read` (cells), `excel_query` (filter rows; min/max cell), attachments (`_prepare_attachments(sources=)`, only the excerpts `rag_block(shown_out=)` showed). Marks only when the tool context carries `source_turn` (both chat lanes); an agent run writes none until 30-c. A remembered (cached) read writes marks for the new turn. At the reply: `link_turn_reply` (off the loop) then `with_linked_head` just before `append_inline_media`, in BOTH lanes; a figure with no mark that is in anything the model was given (`given_figures(system, msgs)`) stays plain, only one found nowhere is `#source/none` (none at all when the model was shown a picture); a `#source/` link the model wrote is always stripped, by the address the page would RESOLVE (`<…>`, `\#`, `&#35;`, nested brackets, a line break in the words or before the address or title, reference definitions, in a blockquote too); code (a fenced or indented block: `_line_kinds`, one classifier for stripping and for linking) is left exactly as written; no link lands in code, a path or a file name; a list item indented four spaces is words, an indented code block is not. Every reader of a SAVED reply as text reads it through `without_figure_links`: the phone (`comm/inbound`, `POST /comm/threads/{id}/send`), the history to the model (`chat_turn._plan_context` → `history_without_figure_links`), history search (`search/index._docs_for_thread` indexes the words), a round given the chat (`agents/threads.run_round(chat_history=)`: the page's panel, a chat handed to another computer), `chat_refs`, the recap check (an id's digits are no number on record), the chat's Share (`routes/chat._share_transcript`), and the voice (`lib/useTTS` `speak`/`speakMore` read the words: the stream is plain and the done frame linked, so the last flush must count the same characters). A model is not meant to see a record id; where a reader not listed here still hands one over, the page opens only a record whose key equals the link words' key. A CSV figure's place is its RECORD `{row, col}` (`_read_csv(layout=)`), never a text line. Dashboard: `lib/sourceLink.ts` (twin, pinned; `figureKey` pinned to `core/numbers` by `__tests__/fixtures/figure-keys-v1549.json`), `components/SourceLink.tsx` (one `OPEN_PLACE_EVENT`, answered by the chat page; elsewhere the place is said in words; opens only a record whose key is the link words' key), `DocPreview` `at` (a changed file is said in the place header and lights nothing by position). OPEN: OCR merged into native pages gets no marks; a rotated PDF page's box is not checked; Word paragraphs light the figure (the frame runs no script, so no scroll); the record has no cap beyond its chat (a remembered read writes up to 3,000 rows again each turn); the in-process pdfium render (`page_image.py`) is not yet checked on the frozen build (pyinstaller-hooks-contrib ships `hook-pypdfium2_raw.py`; a missing DLL would show only as "The page could not be drawn."); `lib/sourceLink.withoutPlaceLinks` (Copy message, the voice) still strips inside code. Pins: `tests/test_leap30a_marks.py`, `tests/test_leap30a_link_reply.py` (`GET /sources` `changed` and a refused file, a link before the turn starts, both lanes), `tests/test_leap30a_page_image.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-30a-source-link.test.tsx`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-30a-chat-page.test.tsx`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-30a-voice.test.tsx`.

- **A scanned pile is sorted from a PLAN the user confirms on its card; its pages are read on this PC first, and a page this PC could not read reaches a model only on the card's press, to the model the card named** (v1.556.0, idea 31-a, D-31.1, D-31.2). `documents/stack.py`: `read_pages` (the text layer, else Windows' OCR through `local_ocr.read_pages`, `OCR_CHUNK` pages per worker; a white page is `blank`, a page neither could read is `unread`), `boundary_signals` (page k of n, a letterhead or sender that changes, a new date, after a blank page: hints only), ONE bounded planning call (`_ask_model`, the `extract` role, `PLAN_CALL_TIMEOUT_S`, page text is data, `core/jsonish.loads_object`; the demo model and a Local only refusal are said in words), then `safe_plan` BY CODE whatever the model said: every page in exactly one document (the first claim wins), each run of pages left out becomes "Not sure (pages 41-42).pdf", a blank page stays with the document before it (`blank`), names and folders cleaned by the work folder's rule and masked. No page read = no model asked. A plan is a JSON file under `<home>/stack_plans/` (`PLAN_DAYS`, swept on save). Tools (`documents/stack_tools.py`): `stack_plan` (allow, READONLY, untrusted output; its card rides `config_cards` kind `stack` via `chat_turn.config_cards_from_result`, so both lanes carry it) and `stack_apply` (ask, REVERSIBLE; no lane arms it for the model: the card's Confirm runs it through `registry.invoke` in `routes/stack.py` with `session_allow={"stack_apply"}` for that call, so a Never run stays refused). `stack_apply` refuses a plan made in the same turn, another folder's plan, a plan already written, a changed scan, an edit that drops or doubles a page or names a folder outside the chat's folder (`folder_problem`); `write_plan` is all or nothing (`pdf_pages.arrange` per document, re-opened, counts add up, the scan's hash checked before and after, never over an existing file: "name (2).pdf"); its Undo is ONE `files_delete` envelope (capture_undo filled in execute, hashes per file) plus the folders it made when empty, and it drops the files' kept marks. Each new file's figures are `sourcemark.kept` rows with the page in the NEW file (`keep_facts`). Chat: `chat_turn.stack_turn` (Auto tools on, not denied, `autoselect.wants_stack` with a PDF attached, carried or named) arms `stack_plan` in `_resolve_armed_tools` AND makes `_prepare_attachments` skip the vision transcription of that PDF (`STACK_HELD_NOTE`, `extract_for_rag_async(held_note=)`), so no page leaves before the card says how many could not be read. Read more: `POST /documents/stack/{id}/read-more` sends only the unread pages, by name to `vision_choice`'s model (vision role, else the first connected model that sees; never one Local only refuses), and answers `changed` (nothing sent) when that choice is no longer the provider the card named. OPEN: confirming by typing in chat is not wired (the card is the way); kept marks are not yet read by a later turn's links (30-a links only a turn's own reads); dates and names are not kept as marks; a cut-off `stack_apply` (Stop or the deadline while its worker thread writes) keeps no Undo; the page strip shows numbers and first words, not page pictures. Pins: `tests/test_leap31a_boundaries.py`, `tests/test_leap31a_apply.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-31a-stack-card.test.tsx`.
